findings.message: Knowledge Duplication — Toolchain path is hardcoded in the step and also set per row in the matrix. Symptom: In `.github/workflows/ci.yaml:189`, the "Setup MinGW path" step always runs `echo "C:/mingw32/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH`, for every `mingw == 'yes'` row. The matrix rows already set different prefixes: `mingw_prefix=C:/mingw64` at line 132 and `mingw_prefix=C:/mingw32` at line 144. So the x86_64 GCC job also gets `C:/mingw32/bin` put at the front of its PATH. Source: The Pragmatic Programmer — DRY; A Philosophy of Software Design — Information Leakage Consequence: The toolchain location is now defined in two places that already disagree. If `C:/mingw32/bin` exists on the runner, any tool SCons calls without a prefix (such as `gcc`, `ar` or `windres`) in the x86_64 job could come from the 32-bit toolchain instead. The next person to change a prefix has to know to update both places. Remedy: Add a matrix key such as `mingw_bin: C:/mingw64/bin` or `C:/mingw32/bin` to each row, and use `echo "${{ matrix.mingw_bin }}" >> $GITHUB_PATH`. You could also build `mingw_prefix` in `flags` from the same key so the path lives in one place.

Change Propagation — The 32-bit GCC toolchain is assumed to exist but nothing installs it. Symptom: The removed `msys2/setup-msys2` step used to install `mingw-w64-i686-gcc`. Nothing replaces it. The x86_32 job now relies on `C:/mingw32` already being on the `windows-2025` image. As far as I know, GitHub's Windows images include only the x86_64 MinGW in `C:\mingw64`; I couldn't check the runner from here. Source: Software Engineering at Google — Dependency Management (an undeclared dependency on the environment) Consequence: If `C:/mingw32` isn't on the image, the "🏁 Windows - MinGW/GCC (MSVCRT) x86_32" job fails at compile time. Even if it is there now, a future image update could remove it without warning, because the workflow never declares that it needs it. Remedy: Install the i686 toolchain explicitly in the x86_32 row, for example by downloading a pinned MinGW-w64 i686 release the same way the llvm-mingw step does. Or confirm the path from a CI run and add a comment citing the runner-image documentation.

Accidental Complexity — Leftover MSYS2 matrix keys. Symptom: Lines 134–135 and 146–147 still set `msys: mingw64/mingw32` and `msysenv: x86_64/i686`. The only step that used them (`setup-msys2`) was deleted. Source: Refactoring — Speculative Generality / dead configuration Consequence: A reader will assume MSYS2 is still involved in these builds, and the keys look like the place to change the architecture when they actually do nothing. Remedy: Remove `msys` and `msysenv` from both GCC matrix rows. ---
